verses.zh: 过了许久，到第三年，耶和华的话临到以利亚说：「你去，使亚哈得见你；我要降雨在地上。」
verses.en: Some time later, in the third year of the famine,[NOTE:1] the Lord’s message came to Elijah, “Go, make an appearance before Ahab, so I may send rain on the surface of the ground.”
notes: The words “of the famine” do not appear in the original text but are supplied for clarification.

verses.zh: 以利亚就去，要使亚哈得见他。那时，撒马利亚有大饥荒；
verses.en: So Elijah went to make an appearance before Ahab.Now the famine was severe in Samaria.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map2-B1; Map4-D3; Map5-E2; Map6-A4; Map7-C1.

verses.zh: 亚哈将他的家宰俄巴底召了来。（俄巴底甚是敬畏耶和华，
verses.en: So Ahab summoned Obadiah, who supervised the palace. (Now Obadiah was a very loyal follower of the Lord.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “now Obadiah greatly feared the Lord.” “Fear” refers here to obedience and allegiance, the products of healthy respect for the Lord’s authority.

verses.zh: 耶洗别杀耶和华众先知的时候，俄巴底将一百个先知藏了，每五十人藏在一个洞里，拿饼和水供养他们。）
verses.en: When Jezebel was killing[NOTE:1] the Lord’s prophets, Obadiah took 100 prophets and hid them in two caves in two groups of 50. He also brought them food and water.)
notes: Heb “cutting off.”

verses.zh: 亚哈对俄巴底说：「我们走遍这地，到一切水泉旁和一切溪边，或者找得着青草，可以救活骡马，免得绝了牲畜。」
verses.en: Ahab told Obadiah, “Go through the land to all the springs and valleys. Maybe we can find some grazing areas[NOTE:1] so we can keep the horses and mules alive and not have to kill[NOTE:2] some of the animals.”
notes: Heb “grass.”
Heb “to cut off.”

verses.zh: 于是二人分地游行，亚哈独走一路，俄巴底独走一路。
verses.en: They divided up the land between them to search it; Ahab went one way by himself and Obadiah went the other way by himself.

verses.zh: 俄巴底在路上恰与以利亚相遇，俄巴底认出他来，就俯伏在地，说：「你是我主以利亚不是？」
verses.en: As Obadiah was traveling along, Elijah met him.[NOTE:1] When he recognized him, he fell facedown to the ground and said, “Is it really you, my master, Elijah?”
notes: Heb “look, Elijah [came] to meet him.”

verses.zh: 回答说：「是。你去告诉你主人说，以利亚在这里。」
verses.en: He replied, “Yes,[NOTE:1] go and say to your master, ‘Elijah is back.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “[It is] I.”
Heb “Look, Elijah”; or “Elijah is here.”

verses.zh: 俄巴底说：「仆人有甚么罪，你竟要将我交在亚哈手里，使他杀我呢？
verses.en: Obadiah[NOTE:1] said, “What sin have I committed that you are ready to hand your servant over to Ahab for execution?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Obadiah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “to kill me.”

verses.zh: 我指着永生耶和华―你的　神起誓，无论哪一邦哪一国，我主都打发人去找你。若说你没有在那里，就必使那邦那国的人起誓说，实在是找不着你。
verses.en: As certainly as the Lord your God lives, my master has sent to every nation and kingdom in an effort to find you. When they say, ‘He’s not here,’ he makes them[NOTE:1] swear an oath that they could not find you.
notes: Heb “he makes the kingdom or the nation swear an oath.”

verses.zh: 现在你说，要去告诉你主人说，以利亚在这里；
verses.en: Now you say, ‘Go and say to your master, “Elijah is back.”’[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Look, Elijah”; or “Elijah is here.”

verses.zh: 恐怕我一离开你，耶和华的灵就提你到我所不知道的地方去。这样，我去告诉亚哈，他若找不着你，就必杀我；仆人却是自幼敬畏耶和华的。
verses.en: But when I leave you, the Lord’s Spirit will carry you away so I can’t find you.[NOTE:1] If I go tell Ahab I’ve seen you, he won’t be able to find you and he will kill me.[NOTE:2] That would not be fair,[NOTE:3] because your servant has been a loyal follower of[NOTE:4] the Lord from my youth.
notes: Heb “to [a place] which I do not know.”
Heb “and I will go to inform Ahab and he will not find you and he will kill me.”
The words “that would not be fair” are added to clarify the logic of Obadiah’s argument.
Heb “has feared the Lord” (also see the note at 1 Kgs 18:3).

verses.zh: 耶洗别杀耶和华众先知的时候，我将耶和华的一百个先知藏了，每五十人藏在一个洞里，拿饼和水供养他们，岂没有人将这事告诉我主吗？
verses.en: Certainly my master is aware of what I did[NOTE:1] when Jezebel was killing the Lord’s prophets. I hid 100 of the Lord’s prophets in two caves in two groups of 50 and I brought them food and water.
notes: Heb “Has it not been told to my master what I did…?” The rhetorical question expects an answer, “Of course it has!”

verses.zh: 现在你说，要去告诉你主人说，以利亚在这里，他必杀我。」
verses.en: Now you say, ‘Go and say to your master, “Elijah is back,”’[NOTE:1] but he will kill me.”
notes: Heb “Look, Elijah”; or “Elijah is here.”

verses.zh: 以利亚说：「我指着所事奉永生的万军之耶和华起誓，我今日必使亚哈得见我。」
verses.en: But Elijah said, “As certainly as the Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:1] lives (whom I serve),[NOTE:2] I will make an appearance before him today.”
notes: Traditionally, “the Lord of Hosts.”
Heb “(before whom I stand).”

verses.zh: 于是俄巴底去迎着亚哈，告诉他；亚哈就去迎着以利亚。
verses.en: When Obadiah went and informed Ahab, the king went to meet Elijah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Obadiah went to meet Ahab and told him, and Ahab went to meet Elijah.”

verses.zh: 亚哈见了以利亚，便说：「使以色列遭灾的就是你吗？」
verses.en: When Ahab saw Elijah, he[NOTE:1] said to him, “Is it really you, the one who brings disaster on[NOTE:2] Israel?”
notes: Heb “Ahab.”
Or “brings trouble on.”

verses.zh: 以利亚说：「使以色列遭灾的不是我，乃是你和你父家；因为你们离弃耶和华的诫命，去随从巴力。
verses.en: Elijah[NOTE:1] replied, “I have not brought disaster on[NOTE:2] Israel. But you and your father’s dynasty have, by abandoning the Lord’s commandments and following the Baals.
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Or “brought trouble on.”

verses.zh: 现在你当差遣人，招聚以色列众人和事奉巴力的那四百五十个先知，并耶洗别所供养事奉亚舍拉的那四百个先知，使他们都上迦密山去见我。」
verses.en: Now send out messengers[NOTE:1] and assemble all Israel before me at Mount Carmel, as well as the 450 prophets of Baal and 400 prophets of Asherah whom Jezebel supports.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The word “messengers” is supplied in the translation both here and in v. 20 for clarification.
Heb “who eat at the table of Jezebel.”

verses.zh: 亚哈就差遣人招聚以色列众人和先知都上迦密山。
verses.en: Ahab sent messengers to all the Israelites and had the prophets assemble at Mount Carmel.

verses.zh: 以利亚前来对众民说：「你们心持两意要到几时呢？若耶和华是　神，就当顺从耶和华；若巴力是　神，就当顺从巴力。」众民一言不答。
verses.en: Elijah approached all the people and said, “How long are you going to be paralyzed by indecision?[NOTE:1] If the Lord is the true God,[NOTE:2] then follow him, but if Baal is, follow him!” But the people did not say a word.
notes: Heb “How long are you going to limp around on two crutches?” (see HALOT 762 s.v. סְעִפִּים). In context this idiomatic expression refers to indecision rather than physical disability.
Heb “the God.”

verses.zh: 以利亚对众民说：「作耶和华先知的只剩下我一个人；巴力的先知却有四百五十个人。
verses.en: Elijah said to them:[NOTE:1] “I am the only prophet of the Lord who is left, but there are 450 prophets of Baal.
notes: Heb “to the people.”

verses.zh: 当给我们两只牛犊，巴力的先知可以挑选一只，切成块子，放在柴上，不要点火；我也预备一只牛犊放在柴上，也不点火。
verses.en: Let them bring us two bulls. Let them choose one of the bulls for themselves, cut it up into pieces, and place it on the wood. But they must not set it on fire. I will do the same to the other bull and place it on the wood. But I will not set it on fire.

verses.zh: 你们求告你们神的名，我也求告耶和华的名。那降火显应的　神，就是　神。」众民回答说：「这话甚好。」
verses.en: Then you[NOTE:1] will invoke the name of your god, and I will invoke the name of the Lord. The god who responds with fire will demonstrate that he is the true God.”[NOTE:2] All the people responded, “This will be a fair test.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Elijah now directly addresses the prophets.
Heb “the God.”
Heb “The matter [i.e., proposal] is good [i.e., acceptable].”

verses.zh: 以利亚对巴力的先知说：「你们既是人多，当先挑选一只牛犊，预备好了，就求告你们神的名，却不要点火。」
verses.en: Elijah told the prophets of Baal, “Choose one of the bulls for yourselves and go first, for you are the majority. Invoke the name of your god, but do not light a fire.”[NOTE:1]
notes: The last sentence of v. 25 is absent in the Syriac Peshitta.

verses.zh: 他们将所得的牛犊预备好了，从早晨到午间，求告巴力的名说：「巴力啊，求你应允我们！」却没有声音，没有应允的。他们在所筑的坛四围踊跳。
verses.en: So they took a bull, as he had suggested,[NOTE:1] and prepared it. They invoked the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying, “Baal, answer us.” But there was no sound and no answer. They jumped[NOTE:2] around on the altar they had made.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and they took the bull which he allowed them.”
Heb “limped” (the same verb is used in v. 21).
The MT has “which he made,” but some medieval Hebrew mss and the ancient versions have the plural form of the verb.

verses.zh: 到了正午，以利亚嬉笑他们，说：「大声求告吧！因为他是神，他或默想，或走到一边，或行路，或睡觉，你们当叫醒他。」
verses.en: At noon Elijah mocked them, “Yell louder! After all, he is a god; he may be deep in thought, or perhaps he stepped out for a moment or has taken a trip. Perhaps he is sleeping and needs to be awakened.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Elijah’s sarcastic proposals would have been especially offensive and irritating to Baal’s prophets, for they believed Baal was imprisoned in the underworld as death’s captive during this time of drought. Elijah’s apparent ignorance of their theology is probably designed for dramatic effect; indeed the suggestion that Baal is away on a trip or deep in sleep comes precariously close to the truth as viewed by the prophets.

verses.zh: 他们大声求告，按着他们的规矩，用刀枪自割、自刺，直到身体流血。
verses.en: So they yelled louder and, in accordance with their prescribed ritual,[NOTE:1] mutilated themselves with swords and spears until their bodies were covered with blood.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “as was their custom.”
Heb “until blood poured out on them.”sn mutilated…covered with blood. This self-mutilation was a mourning rite designed to facilitate Baal’s return from the underworld.

verses.zh: 从午后直到献晚祭的时候，他们狂呼乱叫，却没有声音，没有应允的，也没有理会的。
verses.en: Throughout the afternoon they were in an ecstatic frenzy,[NOTE:1] but there was no sound, no answer, and no response.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “when noon passed they prophesied until the offering up of the offering.”

In 2 Kgs 4:31 the words “there was no sound and there was no response” are used to describe a dead boy. Similar words are used here to describe the god Baal as dead and therefore unresponsive.tc The Old Greek translation and Syriac Peshitta include the following words here: “When it was time to offer the sacrifice, Elijah the Tishbite spoke to the prophets of the abominations: ‘Stand aside for the time being, and I will offer my burnt offering.’ So they stood aside and departed.”

verses.zh: 以利亚对众民说：「你们到我这里来。」众民就到他那里。他便重修已经毁坏耶和华的坛。
verses.en: Elijah then told all the people, “Approach me.” So all the people approached him. He repaired the altar of the Lord that had been torn down.[NOTE:1]
notes: Torn down. The condition of the altar symbolizes the spiritual state of the people.

verses.zh: 以利亚照雅各子孙支派的数目，取了十二块石头（耶和华的话曾临到雅各说：「你的名要叫以色列」），
verses.en: Then Elijah took 12 stones, corresponding to the number of tribes that descended from Jacob, to whom the Lord’s message had come, “Israel will be your name.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Israel will be your name. See Gen 32:28; 35:10.

verses.zh: 用这些石头为耶和华的名筑一座坛，在坛的四围挖沟，可容谷种二细亚，
verses.en: With the stones he constructed an altar for the Lord.[NOTE:1] Around the altar he made a trench large enough to contain two seahs[NOTE:2] of seed.
notes: Heb “and he built the stones into an altar in the name of the Lord.”
A seah was a dry measure equivalent to about seven quarts.

verses.zh: 又在坛上摆好了柴，把牛犊切成块子放在柴上，对众人说：「你们用四个桶盛满水，倒在燔祭和柴上」；
verses.en: He arranged the wood, cut up the bull, and placed it on the wood. Then he said, “Fill four water jars and pour the water on the offering and the wood.”

verses.zh: 又说：「倒第二次。」他们就倒第二次；又说：「倒第三次。」他们就倒第三次。
verses.en: When they had done so,[NOTE:1] he said, “Do it again.” So they did it again. Then he said, “Do it a third time.” So they did it a third time.
notes: The words “when they had done so” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 水流在坛的四围，沟里也满了水。
verses.en: The water flowed down all sides of the altar and filled the trench.

verses.zh: 到了献晚祭的时候，先知以利亚近前来，说：「亚伯拉罕、以撒、以色列的　神，耶和华啊，求你今日使人知道你是以色列的　神，也知道我是你的仆人，又是奉你的命行这一切事。
verses.en: When it was time for the evening offering,[NOTE:1] Elijah the prophet approached the altar[NOTE:2] and prayed: “O Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, prove[NOTE:3] today that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant and have done all these things at your command.
notes: Heb “at the offering up of the offering.”
The words “the altar” are supplied in the translation for clarification.
Heb “let it be known.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你应允我，应允我！使这民知道你―耶和华是　神，又知道是你叫这民的心回转。」
verses.en: Answer me, O Lord, answer me, so these people will know that you, O Lord, are the true God[NOTE:1] and that you are winning back their allegiance.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the God.”
Heb “that you are turning their heart[s] back.”

verses.zh: 于是，耶和华降下火来，烧尽燔祭、木柴、石头、尘土，又烧干沟里的水。
verses.en: Then fire from the Lord fell from the sky.[NOTE:1] It consumed the offering, the wood, the stones, and the dirt, and licked up the water in the trench.
notes: The words “from the sky” are added for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 众民看见了，就俯伏在地，说：「耶和华是　神！耶和华是　神！」
verses.en: When all the people saw this, they threw themselves down with their faces to the ground and said, “The Lord is the true God![NOTE:1] The Lord is the true God!”
notes: Heb “the God” (the phrase occurs twice in this verse).

verses.zh: 以利亚对他们说：「拿住巴力的先知，不容一人逃脱！」众人就拿住他们。以利亚带他们到基顺河边，在那里杀了他们。
verses.en: Elijah told them, “Seize the prophets of Baal! Don’t let even one of them escape!” So they seized them, and Elijah led them down to the Kishon Valley and executed[NOTE:1] them there.
notes: Or “slaughtered.”

verses.zh: 以利亚对亚哈说：「你现在可以上去吃喝，因为有多雨的响声了。」
verses.en: Then Elijah told Ahab, “Go on up and eat and drink, for the sound of a heavy rainstorm can be heard.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for [there is] the sound of the roar of the rain.”

verses.zh: 亚哈就上去吃喝。以利亚上了迦密山顶，屈身在地，将脸伏在两膝之中；
verses.en: So Ahab went on up to eat and drink, while Elijah climbed to the top of Carmel. He bent down toward the ground and put his face between his knees.

verses.zh: 对仆人说：「你上去，向海观看。」仆人就上去观看，说：「没有甚么。」他说：「你再去观看。」如此七次。
verses.en: He told his servant, “Go on up and look in the direction of the sea.” So he went on up, looked, and reported, “There is nothing.”[NOTE:1] Seven times Elijah sent him to look.[NOTE:2]
notes: So he went on up, looked, and reported, “There is nothing.” Several times in this chapter those addressed by Elijah obey his orders. In vv. 20 and 42 Ahab does as instructed, in vv. 26 and 28 the prophets follow Elijah’s advice, and in vv. 30, 34, 40 and 43 the people and servants do as they are told. By juxtaposing Elijah’s commands with accounts of those commands being obeyed, the narrator emphasizes the authority of the Lord’s prophet.
Heb “He said, ‘Return,’ seven times.”

verses.zh: 第七次仆人说：「我看见有一小片云从海里上来，不过如人手那样大。」以利亚说：「你上去告诉亚哈，当套车下去，免得被雨阻挡。」
verses.en: The seventh time the servant[NOTE:1] said, “Look, a small cloud, the size of the palm of a man’s hand, is rising up from the sea.” Elijah[NOTE:2] then said, “Go and tell Ahab, ‘Hitch up the chariots and go down, so that the rain won’t overtake you.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the servant) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “he”; the referent (Elijah) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “so that the rain won’t restrain you.”

verses.zh: 霎时间，天因风云黑暗，降下大雨。亚哈就坐车往耶斯列去了。
verses.en: Meanwhile the sky was covered with dark clouds, the wind blew, and there was a heavy rainstorm. Ahab rode toward[NOTE:1] Jezreel.
notes: Heb “rode and went to.”

verses.zh: 耶和华的灵（原文是手）降在以利亚身上，他就束上腰，奔在亚哈前头，直到耶斯列的城门。
verses.en: Now the Lord energized Elijah with power;[NOTE:1] he tucked his robe into his belt[NOTE:2] and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel.
notes: Heb “and the hand of the Lord was on Elijah.”
Heb “and girded up his loins.” The idea is that of gathering up the robes and tucking them into the sash or belt so that they do not get in the way of the legs when running (or working or fighting).
